maps.name: First Lantern
maps.reason: A compact loop separates movement practice from the exit targets. Establish basic aim, dash and retry comprehension before interpreting choices.

maps.name: The Pilgrim Fork
maps.reason: The straight causeway exposes two firing positions; the statue gallery trades distance for cover. A visible fork makes voluntary exposure interpretable.
maps.confound: Route length and reward must be disclosed

maps.name: Paper Walls
maps.reason: Two hall entrances and screen cover reward checking an angle before committing. The optional archive separates curiosity from mandatory progress.

maps.name: Sanctum of Four Doors
maps.reason: The optional central cut and continuous outer cloister allow a player to enter a threat, reconsider, and leave without a forced dead end.
maps.confound: Central shortcut must not secretly pay more

maps.name: Gutter Run
maps.reason: Two approaches converge at the vent roof. Isolate a single exposure window and compare dash timing or waiting for a safe opening.

maps.name: Chimney Switchbacks
maps.reason: The S-shaped ascent and chimney cover require successive direction changes; the northern bypass provides a deliberate alternative to reactive weaving.
maps.confound: Collision snags must not count as hesitation

maps.name: Twin Eaves
maps.reason: Parallel eaves with a cross-link allow lateral repositioning after a first approach fails. Test a useful switch, not merely frequent movement.
maps.confound: Switch only counts when the original tactic fails

maps.name: Lantern Causeway
maps.reason: A lantern-led boardwalk gives a readable default while the moss island offers exploration. Reveal the rule and landmarks before evaluating a blind approach.

maps.name: Reed Islands
maps.reason: Several islands and a diagonal connector support revising a destination after discovering a blocked lane, rather than memorizing one correct route.

maps.name: Drowned Cloister
maps.reason: The guarded middle crossing and outer ring permit retreat and a new approach; the sheltered island separates regrouping from avoidance.
maps.confound: Refuge use is sensible resource management

maps.name: Orchard Spiral
maps.reason: An outer circuit wraps a tighter shrine loop. Observe whether the player reassesses resources before entering the next layer.
maps.confound: Sunk time is not a reason to reward persistence

maps.name: River of Leaves
maps.reason: The riverbank leads to an island refuge and two final approaches. A retry can preserve earned progress while allowing a changed approach.

maps.name: Last Harvest
maps.reason: The field bypass, return spur and grove refuge provide multiple chances to continue, regroup or stop during a longer encounter.

maps.name: Blue Approach
maps.reason: Broad lanes create recovery room to learn stopping distance before precision is demanded. This is the slip-condition calibration, not a bravery test.

maps.name: Split Glacier
maps.reason: Broad shelves and a central spur allow the same destination through different turn sequences. Check transfer of braking or visibility learning.

maps.name: The Mountain Pass
maps.reason: A pass encounter, high ridge and eastern recovery loop separate a local setback from restarting the whole climb.
maps.confound: Elevation is visual, not a jump mechanic

maps.name: The Joined Roads
maps.reason: Mixed cover and connected routes combine previously isolated decisions. Use as a held-out transfer layout after learning, not as calibration.
maps.confound: Many simultaneous demands prevent single-cause attribution

maps.name: Shroud at Dawn
maps.reason: Three seals and two refuges support repeated bounded recovery decisions. The optional field route prevents the final challenge being only a corridor endurance test.
maps.confound: Session length; never force a failure to elicit a response
